title: Zipline
name: zipline
description: File sharing and screenshot host that works with ShareX, Flameshot and the like, with a link shortener, text pastes, folders, and files that can expire, need a password or delete themselves after so many views. Source: https://github.com/diced/zipline

env.name: ZIPLINE_SECRET
env.label: Secret (required)
env.description: At least 32 characters. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or every login and upload token stops working.

env.name: ZIPLINE_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or Zipline can't reach its database.

env.name: ZIPLINE_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set both secrets before you deploy (openssl rand -hex 32 makes good ones), since the stack won't start without them, and keep them the same when you redeploy. Then open http://<your-host>:3200 (or whichever port you picked) and create the first account, which becomes the super admin. There are no open sign-ups, so you add everyone else under Users. Settings, under your name in the top corner, makes ready-to-use ShareX and Flameshot configs. Links use whatever address you opened it on, and the rest of the settings (domains, HTTPS links, sign-ups, the 100 MB file limit) live in the dashboard under Server Settings. It checks GitHub for new versions, which you can switch off there under Features. Files and thumbnails live in the zipline-uploads volume, everything else in postgres-data. Docs: zipline.diced.sh
